strings.name: Ban Ki-moon
strings.summary: Ban rose through South Korea’s diplomatic service and served as the eighth UN secretary-general from 2007 to 2016. He supported the multilateral processes behind the Sustainable Development Goals and Paris Agreement, emphasizing climate, gender equality and humanitarian assistance. His tenure also faced Syria’s war, peacekeeping failures and Haiti’s cholera epidemic. Before leaving office he apologized for the UN’s inadequate response in Haiti; accountability and compensation remained disputed.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: As UN secretary-general, he contributed to the Sustainable Development Goals and the Paris climate agreement, and continued international public advocacy afterward.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-01.value: North Chungcheong region, Korea, then under Japanese colonial rule
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Seoul National University, BA in international relations (1970); Harvard University, MPA (1985)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Multilateral climate cooperation
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Promoted international climate mobilization around the 2015 Paris Agreement and its subsequent signing.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: The 2030 Agenda
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Supported negotiations among states on the development agenda with seventeen Sustainable Development Goals.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Continued multilateral engagement
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Met the president of the UN General Assembly in New York as a former secretary-general.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Ended his UN tenure
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Completed two terms totaling ten years; António Guterres succeeded him the following day.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Apologized over Haiti cholera
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Acknowledged that the UN had not done enough regarding the outbreak and its spread and proposed a new support approach.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Paris Agreement adopted
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Parties adopted the global climate agreement during his sustained climate diplomacy.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Sustainable Development Goals adopted
strings.timeline.event-05.text: UN member states adopted the 2030 Agenda and its seventeen interlinked goals.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Became UN secretary-general
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Succeeded Kofi Annan as the eighth secretary-general and was appointed to a second term in 2011.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Became South Korea’s foreign minister
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Served as minister of foreign affairs and trade before entering the UN secretary-general selection.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Earned an MPA
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Completed a master’s degree at Harvard’s Kennedy School of Government.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Entered the diplomatic service
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Graduated in international relations from Seoul National University and entered South Korea’s foreign ministry.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Korea
strings.timeline.event-10.text: His childhood included the upheaval of the Korean War before his later diplomatic career.
